newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada services deficit drops again in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Canada services deficit drops again in 1996.

text.p: Canada's deficit in its trade in services dropped in 1996, marking the third decline in a row, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
It said the deficit fell by C$500 million to a deficit of C$9.9 billion, the first time this decade that it was below C$10 billion.
Canada exported a record C$39 billion in services. It imported a record C$49 billion, a figure that increased less rapidly than exports.

Transportation services led the way, its deficit falling C$600 million to C$3.1 billion, reflecting lower deficits in air- and water-borne transportation and higher earnings in the United States for Canadian-domiciled truckers.
The deficit in commercial services was unchanged at C$4.0 billion.
Spending by incoming and outgoing travelers each grew by more than C$1 billion. The deficit rose slightly to C$3.0 billion but was less than half its 1992 peak of C$6.4 billion.
